Action Plan:
1. Provide prescription for stronger analgesia: offer either  
   • Ibuprofen up-titration (up to 400 mg 3 × daily) OR  
   • Naproxen (dose/route/frequency not documented) ± Paracetamol or Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
2. Educate on correct NSAID dosing, advise adding Paracetamol and/or Codeine only if needed.  
3. Begin a headache diary to identify frequency and potential triggers (stress, hydration, screen time, light exposure).  
4. Arrange review in 1–2 weeks; earlier if worsening pain, new neurological deficits, visual loss, or persistent photophobia.  
5. Discuss possible prophylactic migraine therapy at follow-up if headaches recur or increase in frequency.  
6. Recommend formal eye examination to assess for refractive changes or screen-related eye strain.  
7. General advice: maintain adequate hydration, limit screen brightness, manage stress, avoid known migraine triggers.  
8. Safety-netting: seek urgent care for sudden vision loss, weakness, speech difficulty, severe unremitting headache, or fever/neck stiffness.  
9. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting complaint: 3-day history of progressively worsening headache, rated 8/10, dull→intermittently sharp, diffuse but maximal around right eye; constant with fluctuating intensity.  
• Associated symptoms: photophobia, brief “shooting lights,” nausea without vomiting, difficulty focusing at work.  
• Denies: visual loss, persistent blurry vision, neck stiffness, fever, rash, focal weakness, speech difficulty, head trauma.  
• Aggravating factors: bright light, screen time.  
• Relieving factors tried: Ibuprofen (3 tablets/day for 2 days) – minimal relief.  
• Past medical history: none reported.  
• Family history: mother & sister with frequent migraines.  
• Medications: none regular; recent Ibuprofen (dose unspecified, 3 tablets/day).  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Social history: lives with 3 housemates; works in IT (prolonged computer use); socially smokes & drinks; moderate work stress; wears glasses (no recent eye test).

Objective:
• No examination findings or vitals documented.  
• No investigations performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache (likely migraine):
   - Assessment: Clinical picture and positive family history suggest migraine-type headache.
   - Differential: Tension-type headache, cluster headache, medication-overuse headache, secondary causes (low probability given absence of red flags).
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; headache diary to monitor pattern & triggers.
   - Treatment planned: Optimize NSAID dosing (Ibuprofen up to 400 mg TID or switch to Naproxen), consider adding Paracetamol or Codeine for breakthrough pain.
   - Follow-up: Review in 1–2 weeks; earlier if red-flag symptoms. Consider prophylactic therapy next visit if recurrent.

2. Eye strain / need for vision assessment:
   - Assessment: Photophobia and prolonged screen use; no recent eye exam.
   - Investigations planned: Routine optometry assessment.
   - Treatment planned: Reduce screen brightness, regular screen breaks, ensure corrective lenses up to date.
   - Referrals: Optometrist for comprehensive eye test.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Vital signs, focused neurological & ocular examination, exact analgesic dosing instructions.  
● Internal conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor hesitations but clinically intelligible.
